# QWEN IMAGE EDIT 2.1 TURBO — MODELS & NODES

## 1. Shared models — required

These three files are shared by text-to-image, editing, inpainting and outpainting. Download them once. All folders below are inside your **ComfyUI** folder.

**Diffusion model → `models/diffusion_models/`**
- [Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo-v0.2.1-6step-int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo/blob/main/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo-v0.2.1-6step-int8_convrot.safetensors?download=true)

**Text / vision encoder → `models/text_encoders/`**
- [qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors?download=true)

**Texture-fix VAE → `models/vae/`**
- [texture_fix_vae_for_qwen_image_2.1_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/texture-fix-vae-for-qwen-image-2.1/resolve/main/texture_fix_vae_for_qwen_image_2.1_bf16.safetensors?download=true)

## 2. Feature-specific models

Only needed when using the corresponding feature.

**ControlNet Union → `models/model_patches/`**
- [qwen_image_2.1_fun_controlnet_union_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1/resolve/main/model_patches/qwen_image_2.1_fun_controlnet_union_int8_convrot.safetensors?download=true)

**Outpainting → `models/loras/`**
- [qwen-image-2.1-outpaint-v2.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/ausboss/Qwen-Image-2.1-Outpaint-LoRA/resolve/main/qwen-image-2.1-outpaint-v2.safetensors?download=true)

The outpainting loader is configured for this v2 adapter. Ordinary crop-and-stitch inpainting does not require a separate inpainting checkpoint.

## 3. Optional task LoRAs

Put these in **`models/loras/`**. They are options already listed in the workflow, not files that must all be enabled together.

**Head replacement**
- [bfs_head_v1.1_qwen_2.1.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Alissonerdx/BFS-Best-Face-Swap/resolve/main/bfs_head_v1.1_qwen_2.1.safetensors?download=true)

**Body replacement**
- [bfs_body_swap_v1.0_qwen_2.1.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Alissonerdx/BFS-Best-Face-Swap/resolve/main/bfs_body_swap_v1.0_qwen_2.1.safetensors?download=true)

**Bounding-box object removal**
- [Qwen-Image-2.1-Object-Remover-Bbox-turbo-4000.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/prithivMLmods/Qwen-Image-2.1-Object-Remover-Bbox-turbo/resolve/main/Qwen-Image-2.1-Object-Remover-Bbox-turbo-4000.safetensors?download=true)

**Bounding-box object movement**
- [Qwen-Image-2.1-Object-Mover-Bbox-turbo-4000.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/prithivMLmods/Qwen-Image-2.1-Object-Mover-Bbox-turbo/resolve/main/Qwen-Image-2.1-Object-Mover-Bbox-turbo-4000.safetensors?download=true)

The word “turbo” is part of those two object-adapter filenames; it does not mean this workflow includes a separate turbo acceleration LoRA.

## 4. Optional text-to-image LoRAs

Put these in **`models/loras/`**. All three entries start OFF in the saved text-to-image LoRA loader.

**Qwen Image 2.1 Fix**
- [qwen-image-2.1-fix-1.0-comfy.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/e-n-v-y/Qwen-Image-2.1-Fix/resolve/main/qwen-image-2.1-fix-1.0-comfy.safetensors?download=true)
- [Author's model card and settings](https://huggingface.co/e-n-v-y/Qwen-Image-2.1-Fix)

**Lenovo UltraReal — Qwen 2.1 version**
- [lenovo_qwen21.safetensors — community-mirror download](https://huggingface.co/cdkkkk/setup/resolve/main/qwen21/lenovo_qwen21.safetensors?download=true)
- [Creator's model page — v1.0 Qwen2.1](https://civitai.com/models/1662740?modelVersionId=3349565)

The download above is a community mirror, not the creator's own repository. Use the Qwen 2.1 file, not the older `lenovo.safetensors` for the original Qwen Image model.

**NiceGirls UltraReal — Qwen 2.1 version**
- [nicegirls_qwen12.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/RunningHubAI/rh-nicegirls-ultrareal-qwen-2.1-lora/resolve/main/nicegirls_qwen12.safetensors?download=true)
- [Publisher's model card](https://huggingface.co/RunningHubAI/rh-nicegirls-ultrareal-qwen-2.1-lora)

## 5. Custom node packs

Install the missing packs through **ComfyUI Manager**, or follow their repository installation instructions. Restart ComfyUI and refresh the browser afterward. The packs below supply this workflow’s node types; RES4LYF supplies its selected text-to-image sampler.

- **[rgthree-comfy](https://github.com/rgthree/rgthree-comfy)** — `Power Lora Loader (rgthree)`, `Image Comparer (rgthree)`, `Fast Groups Muter (rgthree)`, `Fast Groups Bypasser (rgthree)` and `Label (rgthree)`.
- **[ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes)** — `SetNode` / `GetNode` connections for the shared model, text encoder and VAE.
- **[ComfyUI-AusBoss](https://github.com/ausboss/ComfyUI-AusBoss)** — `AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadImagePad`, `AUSBOSS_NODES_CropForInpaint` and `AUSBOSS_NODES_StitchInpaint` (Load Image + Pad, Crop For Inpaint and Stitch Inpaint).
- **[comfyui_controlnet_aux](https://github.com/Fannovel16/comfyui_controlnet_aux)** — `AIO_Preprocessor`, used to prepare ControlNet maps.
- **[ComfyUI-PixelDriftFix](https://github.com/Mozer/ComfyUI-PixelDriftFix)** — `PixelDriftFix`, inside the PIXEL DRIFT FIXER subgraph.
- **[RES4LYF](https://github.com/ClownsharkBatwing/RES4LYF)** — registers the **`res_2s` sampler selected in TEXT TO IMAGE**. It is needed for those saved settings even though the visible node is the standard `KSampler`.

- **[ComfyUI-Fantastic-MiniMaxH3-PromptBuilder](https://github.com/Adudeguyman/ComfyUI-Fantastic-MiniMaxH3-PromptBuilder)** — `MiniMaxH3MediaLoader` / `MiniMaxH3ReferenceSplitter`, displayed as **Fantastic H3 Media Loader** and **Fantastic H3 Reference Splitter**. Used for the nine-picture input in MULTI-EDIT. No MiniMax model weights are needed for loading pictures.
- **[ComfyUI_essentials](https://github.com/cubiq/ComfyUI_essentials)** — `BatchCount+` and `ImageBatchMultiple+`. These existing utilities let empty reference slots pass safely through the reference-size subgraph and prompt-enhancer batching. No locally written Python nodes are required.

Install all eight to retain the complete workflow as supplied. Optional features may be bypassed, but their custom node definitions still belong to this JSON.

## 6. Native ComfyUI nodes — no separate node pack

Use a ComfyUI installation with native Qwen Image 2.1 and subgraph support. The saved core-node metadata is `0.38.0`; this is a recorded version, not a separately verified minimum.

The following native node types are present, including inside subgraphs:

- **Model loading / cache:** `UNETLoader`, `CLIPLoader`, `VAELoader`, `QwenImage21Cache`, `ModelPatchLoader`.
- **Conditioning / generation:** `TextEncodeQwenImage21`, `ZImageFunControlnet`, `EmptyLatentImage`, `KSampler`, `VAEDecode`.
- **Images / transparency:** `LoadImage`, `ImageScaleToTotalPixels`, `JoinImageWithAlpha`, `SplitImageWithAlpha`, `BatchImagesNode`.
- **Prompt enhancement / text logic:** `TextGenerate`, `JsonExtractString`, `StringCompare`, `StringFormat`, `PrimitiveStringMultiline`, `PrimitiveBoolean`, `ComfySwitchNode`.
- **Output / documentation:** `SaveImage`, `PreviewImage`, `PreviewAny`, `Note`, `MarkdownNote`.

The UUID-named nodes are embedded subgraphs included in this workflow, not additional repositories to install.

## 7. Prompt enhancement and automatic downloads

**Prompt enhancement:** this version uses native `TextGenerate` and text-processing nodes with the shared **qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors** encoder. This JSON does **not** select a separate Qwen3.5 PE checkpoint and does **not** require the old PromptEnhancer-MTP node pack.

**ControlNet preprocessors:** the saved AIO choice is `OpenposePreprocessor`. Its node pack downloads `body_pose_model.pth`, `hand_pose_model.pth` and `facenet.pth` through its own checkpoint-download helper when needed. These are preprocessor weights, not the Qwen Union checkpoint. Let the node manage them; an internet connection is needed for an uncached first run. Other AIO presets can have their own weight downloads.

Only the models and node packs used by this JSON are listed here. Model and extension licenses remain those of their respective publishers.

## 8. MULTI-EDIT — nine-picture Media Loader

Put the working image in **Picture 1**, then add up to eight references in Pictures 2–9. The nine picture outputs are already connected. Empty slots are ignored automatically: no reference-group toggles are needed. Removing, reordering, or disabling a picture compacts the numbering of the active pictures.

Use Qwen’s **`<image1>` … `<image9>`** tags in your instruction, not H3’s `<Picture 1>` tags. The prompt enhancer receives the same active pictures in the same order. Videos, soundtracks and audio outputs are deliberately unconnected; load pictures only.

**Sizing:** the main image keeps the existing Scale Image to Total Pixels node and its existing bypass control. Reference Image Sizes is an embedded subgraph made of existing nodes, not a new extension. It keeps Picture 2 at 0.59 MP and Pictures 3–9 at 1 MP by default; change the per-picture values there as needed. Qwen’s encoder remains at resolution = 0, preserving those prepared dimensions. More references use more memory and processing.

**Input transparency:** the upstream H3 Media Loader converts pictures to RGB and does not preserve PNG input alpha. Keep the original Load Image workflow for edits that need transparent input pixels. This change does not replace the output VAE, and it does not change the inpainting or outpainting branches.

**Installer dependency:** the previous Qwen installers did not include the Fantastic H3 or Essentials packs. Install them through Manager if missing; links are above. Restart ComfyUI and refresh the browser. Users who already installed these packs for earlier workflows do not need another copy.

# Edit Prompt Enhancer — General (v2, 精简版)

**FIRST — there are TWO separate language decisions. Do NOT conflate them.**

**(A) Language of the rewritten prompt's DESCRIPTIVE prose — every word OUTSIDE double quotes (the description you write for the diffusion model, NOT the text painted into the image). This decision is final and non-negotiable:**
- User instruction is in Chinese → write the description in Chinese.
- User instruction is in English → write the description in English.
- User instruction is in ANY other language (Japanese, Korean, French, Spanish, Thai, etc.) → write the description in English.

**(B) Language of the TEXT THAT WILL BE RENDERED INTO THE OUTPUT IMAGE — the content INSIDE double quotes. Decide it in this strict priority order:**
1. If the user's instruction gives the exact text to write, OR names a target language for the text (e.g. "改成'夏日特惠'", "把标题写成英文", "add a Japanese title", "write the caption in Thai") → render exactly that text / in exactly that specified language.
2. Otherwise, if the input image already contains text → render in the DOMINANT language of the image's existing text — even when the instruction is written in a different language.
3. Otherwise (the image contains no text AND the instruction names no target language) → render in the language of the user's instruction itself — including Japanese, Korean, Thai, Arabic, French, etc. Do NOT force it to English.
Worked example: image is mostly Thai, instruction is in English asking to add/redesign a title without giving the exact words or a language → the rendered (quoted) text must be **Thai** (the image's dominant language), while the surrounding description (A) is still written in English.

Two reinforcements on decision (B): all rendered (quoted) text must be **monolingual** — do not mix Chinese and English inside the quotes and do not emit a bilingual pair unless the user explicitly asks for one. And **genre never overrides input language**: a "spec sheet / cinematic data-document / storyboard / technical parameter" look is achieved through layout and typography, NOT by switching rendered labels to English — every header, label, and caption stays in the decided language (standardized units and user-given proper nouns may remain Latin).

You are an expert at clarifying image editing instructions. Given a user's vague or ambiguous edit instruction and the input image(s), rewrite it into a precise, unambiguous, actionable editing directive. An input image is ALWAYS present — this is always an image-editing task, never text-to-image from nothing.

## Core Objective

Rewrite the instruction so a downstream image-editing model can execute it without guessing — anchored on what the input image(s) actually show, faithful to the user's intent, inventing nothing.
